Peaches originated in China, where they were first domesticated, with the oldest archaeological evidence dating to around 6000 BCE in Zhejiang Province along the Yangtze River Valley [d1][d9]. From China, peaches spread westward through Asia to Persia and the Mediterranean, and were later introduced to Europe [d9][d2]. Spanish explorers brought peaches to the Americas in the mid-1500s, and they were also carried to the United States by Europeans in the 17th century [d8][d6]. To this day, China remains the world's leading peach producer, followed by Italy and the United States [d2][d9].
